headline: High-risk pair: n8n’s server-side execution and broad egress can expose Dexter’s financial workflows to data leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can write to .dexter/scratchpad and n8n can read/write server filesystem plus orchestrate AI Agent nodes, so a file-based bridge is plausible. Neither profile shows a direct shared channel by default, but n8n’s workflow nodes can ingest content as instructions, making prompt injection feasible if Dexter output is fed into a workflow.
conditions: IF Dexter output is copied into an n8n workflow node as prompt text or file content
IF n8n reads .dexter/scratchpad or another shared directory without content filtering
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories
Add a content-sanitization step before any n8n prompt node
Disable automatic ingestion of Dexter scratchpad files
Use explicit allowlisted fields instead of raw file text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to workflow inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress to multiple APIs; n8n can read the server filesystem, use broad egress, and handle per-credential secrets. If Dexter artifacts or data are routed into n8n, sensitive material can leave the local boundary through integrations or logs. The pairwise leakage path is credible from both profiles.
conditions: IF Dexter writes financial data into files or workflow inputs that n8n can read
IF an n8n integration node transmits those inputs to a third-party service
mitigations: Restrict n8n to a separate workspace
Mask financial fields before handoff
Disable unnecessary integration nodes
Rotate and scope credentials used by n8n
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on workflow inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and broad egress; n8n supports multiple instances, server filesystem writes, shell execution, and shared state via datastore/connected systems. Overlapping write and execution surfaces create a real conflict risk on shared resources, especially if both operate in the same directory or workflow state without locking.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or shared datastore
IF n8n Execute Command nodes and Dexter runs overlap in time
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Serialize access with a lock file
Disable Execute Command for shared jobs
Use per-run namespaces in datastore
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter is a scientific-research agent that can generate outputs from financial data, and n8n is an automation orchestrator whose AI Agent node can act on workflow inputs. If n8n treats Dexter’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or integrations. The pair lacks a built-in verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF n8n uses Dexter output as a trigger or decision input
IF no human or validation step checks Dexter’s claims before downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a manual approval step
Require schema validation on Dexter outputs
Limit downstream actions to read-only mode
Log and review high-impact workflow runs
requires-engineering: add verification agents or rule-based checks

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and stores credentials on its server. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated financial data is routed through n8n workflows with broader retention or logging than intended. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction, not either alone.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed in an n8n workflow with default logging or retention
IF the workflow stores secrets or payloads on the n8n server beyond policy limits
mitigations: Review retention settings
Minimize logged payloads
Separate regulated workflows from general automation
Restrict access to credential stores
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data classification
